summary: Menominee North Pier Light at the mouth of the Menominee River: a fifth-order pierhead light from 1877 on an octagonal cast-iron tower, electrified in 1927, automated in 1972, now city-owned.

lens.where: museum adjacent to Sand Point Lighthouse, Escanaba

structures.note: Moved 305 ft lakeward in 1881 and 345 ft in 1886; placed on a concrete block in 1927 (LighthouseFriends)
Sixty-foot steel rear range tower about 248 yards from the octagonal light (LighthouseFriends)
Frame building beside the light; removed in the 1927 work
Duplex at the corner of Pengilly and Kirby streets (now 3rd Avenue and 2nd Street); LighthouseFriends says it remains standing

access.note: Reached by walking the pier. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower open in season. The USLHS archive record says 'Open to Public: No'; treated as a conflict.

events.note: Fifth-order fixed red light established on the north pier, 1 January 1877 (LighthouseFriends; the archive gives 1877 as the year of the original lens and the Board's 1891 entry shows the pierhead light already in service)
Elevated walkway extended 623 feet toward shore

Tower moved another 345 feet lakeward; walkway extended

Ten-inch steam whistle established 4 September 1897 (funded by act of 11 June 1896)
Fifteen-foot-square concrete foundation built under the tower

Sixty-foot steel range tower placed 248 yards from the octagonal light; Menominee Pierhead Range Rear listed as established

Deemed excess by the Coast Guard and offered for transfer
Transferred to the City of Menominee
Exterior repainted; interior stripped to plaster and refurbished (begun 2016, funded by an anonymous donor)
Public tours begin August 2017; regular tours from Memorial Day weekend 2018

corrections.why: The record's 1927 date is the date of the 1927 rebuild on a concrete block, not the first lighting. The Board's 1891 report shows a fifth-order light changed to fourth order at this pierhead in September 1891, and LighthouseFriends dates the first fifth-order light to 1 January 1877. The archive's 'Year Tower Established: 1927' is the source of the confusion.

LighthouseFriends describes the tower that stood on the pier in 1877 as octagonal and cast iron, and the archive records 'Tower Construction Material: CAST IRON'. The record's conical masonry brick tower does not match either source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive gives 1877 as the year the station was established and 1927 as the year the tower was established; the National Register gives 1877 and 1927 as significant years. LighthouseFriends says the same octagonal tower was on the pier in 1877 and was set on a new base in 1927. The 1891 Board entry records a fifth-order light changed to fourth order at the pierhead, which does not match the archive's fourth-order original optic. The 1877 date is used, and the story states the disagreement.
The archive says 'Open to Public: No'; LighthouseFriends describes grounds open and the tower open to tours in season. The city's tours are the more recent source and are used.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: official Board entries for 1891, 1895 and 1896 plus the 1916 Bulletin list; LighthouseFriends carries the 1877 first lighting, the 1881 and 1886 moves, the 1884 fire, the 1897 whistle and the 1906 duplex, which are not in any source in the corpus (the Board's 1877-1890 reports are not in the local corpus). The National Register nomination (NRIS 05000738) is not digitised: the served file is a 22 KB placeholder. Newspapers: one Chronicling America search for Menominee pierhead light (MI papers, 1877-1930) returned one unrelated 1891 page; no newspaper is used. The Board indexes label the station 'Menominee Pierhead, Wisconsin' in some years and 'Michigan' in others, and its text says 'Green Bay, Michigan'; the story follows the text. The record's characteristic (Oc R 4s) and focal height were not re-verified against the Light List; the record's 'Oc R 4s' differs from the Fl R 4s printed in some outside sources, which are not used here. Roster: 52 lines copied from the archive as printed, with its own role headings (USCG and laborer included). Names after about 1960 are named only as the archive prints them, with no personal detail. No wreck or rescue is tied to this light in the sources used. The fire of 1884 is from LighthouseFriends only; the story now places it under Storms. The 1881 request for $5,000 for a keeper's dwelling is LighthouseFriends' account, and the story attributes it to LighthouseFriends rather than quoting the Board. The USLHS archive's 'Original Optic Type: FOURTH ORDER' and 'Year Original Lens Installed: 1877' conflict with the 1891 change from fifth to fourth order; the story follows the Board's entry.
